title: One button to add a step: + Add a step, between steps and after the last
boardTitle: DT348: one button to add a step, + Add a step, between steps and after the last

opportunity.from: Coach Milan 23 November 2026, 23:50, looking at the board B165 and B166: + Add a step and + Step here are two different buttons for the same job. 23:59: Next.
opportunity.job: Write a recipe's steps: add a step where it belongs.
opportunity.kind: Two kinds of button for one job: the eye has to learn both.
opportunity.why_now: DT345 (0.3.188) added + Step here between steps; the end of the list still has the older button.

problem: Writing steps, a step between two steps comes from + Step here, a dashed button under the step. A step after the last one comes from + Add a step, a filled button of another kind and another place. Same job, two looks, two words.
story: When I write a recipe's steps, I want one button to add a step wherever it goes, so that I learn it once.
now: Edit recipe, Steps: 1, + Step here (a dashed button, fully round like a chip), 2, then + Add a step (white, blue border, 14 px corners, 36 px high). The publish sheet writes steps with the same editor, so it is the same there.
proposed: Coach Milan 26 November 01:40 to 01:41: one button, + Add a step, the app's outlined action button (white, blue border, 14 px corners, design rule D9), between steps and after the last one; + Step here goes. Each is 44 px high (D10) and sits under its step. Its label for a screen reader says where: Add a step between step 1 and step 2, Add a step after step 2. Enter in a step still adds the next one. One editor (StepsEditor), so Edit recipe and the publish sheet change together.
looked_at: + Step here everywhere, the dashed round button (drawn 25 November 20:50): not chosen, 26 November 01:41: a button says what the tap does (D10), the place shows where; fully round is the look of a chip (D3), and the dashed look is the only one of its kind.
short: + Add a step between steps and after the last, the outlined button; + Step here goes; release 0.3.197

ac.title: One button, between and after
ac.text: Given Banana porridge with 2 steps, when I open Edit recipe, then under step 1 and under step 2 there is + Add a step, the same outlined button, 44 px high, and there is no + Step here

ac.title: It adds step 3
ac.text: Given that, when I tap + Add a step under step 2, then step 3 opens, empty, with the cursor in it, and + Add a step is between step 2 and step 3 and under step 3

ac.title: For a screen reader
ac.text: Given 2 steps, when a screen reader reads the buttons, then they say Add a step between step 1 and step 2 and Add a step after step 2

ac.title: The publish sheet
ac.text: Given the same recipe in the publish sheet, when I read its steps, then the same: + Add a step between and after the last, no + Step here

ac.title: In every language
ac.text: Given Srpski or German, when I open Edit recipe, then every button to add a step has the same words, and its screen reader label is in that language

unchanged: Where a button between steps adds the step (DT345).
Enter in a step adds the next step.
The foods under the steps, and the notes about foods in no step.
Start cooking and the steps as read on the recipe page.
checks: Light plus the German sweep: one component (StepsEditor) and its words. The unit tests; the build; a new walkthrough for AC1 to AC5; the walkthroughs that tap + Step here or + Add a step today (DT345's, day-levels, past-and-plan, recipe-photos, steps-and-parts, explore-photo, tester-fixes) change with the story where they read the button's words, each with a note; deutsch, language and design-rules. About 12 walkthroughs, 5 minutes. Words: steps.stepHere goes; steps.addAfter is new (Srpski and German); steps.addAStep and steps.addBetween stay.
details: src/components/StepsEditor.tsx: the buttons between steps are pill pill-small pill-action st-add st-between with steps.addAStep and the label steps.addBetween; the last has the label steps.addAfter; src/index.css: .st-add 44 px high and under the step (margin-left 34 px); .st-between drops its dashed look.
The pictures: before from main, 0.3.196; new from a scratch build of main with the change, not committed. The publish sheet opens for a coach (chefmealan-coach).
